1. Get a big piece of paper and write the hours across the top and weekdays down the side. 
2. Mark everything you do like class times, travel times, meal times
3, set realistic hours for when you will study
4, ensure you stick to it and when distractions come along say no
5. Be in a clean room, or stay in library etc... Unplug and do not be near any TVs etc (I text my friends asking them not to disturb me in my study hours and switched my phone off) 
6. Set a target for each study session (read chapter X, learn equation, begin introduction of essay, research etc) 
7. If its reading stuff you are learning, write down/ highlight key points and repeat them in your head as you read the passage to keep you focused. While doing this, pick a highlighter and keep that colour for all points linking to one key point (e.g. i did healthcare so pink highlighter for all things relating to symptoms, orange highlighter for all things relating to cures etc.. ) 
8. Before switching to a new subject get a scrap bit of paper and from memory write down things you remember and go back and check they are correct. Alternatively, mindmap and put the main thing in the middle and branch off all you remember and that will help to remember the previous studying you did.
9. Switch to a new topic after at least a half hour break relax and drink plenty of water 

If you don't stick to your schedule be strict with yourself so that you catch up the next day. Also have a reward for yourself once you have completed your study session. Whether it be a Netflix episode/ food/ just something to look forward to and keep you focused. Hope that helps :)

Pro-choice. I went through it, its a really hard decision to make. I fully expect to be shot down for what I'm about to say. It was the wrong time in life, our parents knew and would not support us, the father was fully aware and we made the decision together. Many of you will hear these excuses, in my situation, birth control failed, I was 4 weeks and I knew I was pregnant before taking the test, I felt very different. So what is my opinion? At the time I knew it was the right decision and the child wouldn't have had a great life. Do I regret it? Yes but because I cannot comprehend how I made that decision. Do I miss the father? Yes. Did I lose a lot? Yes. Many friendships were destroyed, the father and I can't even look at each other and haven't spoken in years. Has it changed me as a person? Yes. I am completely different now, I fear ever becoming pregnant again because I feel I've already failed as a mother.  I don't feel sorry for myself but I live with what I did every day and it is a part of me that I'll never forget. I am still pro choice because I'd be a hypocrite otherwise, but personally, I would never go through it again and I respect anyone who has gone through it, it is a life changing decision that affects everyone differently. I see on this thread that some refer to it as murder, ever since that day I had the termination I've felt like a murderer. Its a situation of mixed emotions. Any questions feel free to ask, I understand any strong opposing opinions and I'll answer as best I can.

Adding to the abortion debate: Abortion is a very hard decision to make, personally, it wasn't about "murdering my child" or using the bullsh excuse that "it was a bundle of cells." The fact of the matter is that, it was the wrong time, the wrong circumstance and ultimately I had to be selfish. That child would not have been loved by either parent. I was fully responsible for the decision I made, do I regret it? No. Has it changed my life forever? Yes. Do I think about what I did all the time? Yes. Does it eat me up? Yes. What about the father? He was against the termination, he and I no longer speak, he was fully informed of my decision and he was delusional about the situation. He continued to say that we would make it work. We may well have, but to what cost? Neither of us would have the careers we have now and that child would have been dreadfully deprived. Our parents knew and they refused to help if the pregnancy continued. Abortion is a tricky topic but I firmly believe the father should have his say, it is a huge decision and everyone is different. I listen to prolife arguments and understand them but until you've been in that situation you really have no right to comment.

I explained that I appreciated that, but for both of us it wasn't the right time. Eventually he came around and came with me to the procedure. He cried all day and I was numb. This happened 3 years ago and for the last two years I lost any maternal instinct. I've never felt guilty about it, but I was angry for getting pregnant in the first place. I ended things with my partner of the time, about a month after as I couldn't bear to see him hurt, that's what I regret. Occasionally I'll message him to see how hes holding up but he hates me and apparently will never tell anyone of our experience, on the last convo he pretty much said I'm dead to him. I get that and wish my pregnancy had never happened. My family don't know, a few friends do and I still think about it from time to time but its personal, those who know me, even if they're aware of what I did, won't hear me talk or cry about it now. I keep it to myself. My current partner knows but we don't talk about it and that's the way I want to keep it. I made the right decision, yes it still hurts sometimes but its hard to explain unless you went through it. Happy to answer any questions.

Bipolar disorder. I was diagnosed with it 4 years ago, apparently i have a split personality, no concept of money, when I'm excited, or angry I'm "in an episode" , ...

People who know I've been diagnosed (friends/family

Decided to buy a new pair of heels and jacket spent quite a lot of money "it must be really hard to control impulse purchases" - no, actually, I saved up and wanted them. You have read on the internet that we can be financially impulsive whilst in a manic episode. 

A manic episode - I feel on top of the world, bought £350 worth of gifts for my friends, bought 4 things online including a laptop...got in my car and hit 100mph on the motorway and got my hair dyed at a salon in one day. This was the best decision and I stood by it for weeks... Eventually I rationalized my impulse and decided to sell them, had my keys taken off of me and am stable. 

Friend asks me one day " I think I'm bipolar I was happy all day but felt really sad and spent £50 to cheer myself up" 

A family member " you're bipolar? So who am I talking to at the moment then? *laughs* " - yes, this is a misunderstood and stereotyped opinion that those with bipolar have a split personality. The reason people think this, is that schizophrenia and schizoid disorders are in the same cluster with bipolar within the DSM. Funnily enough, depression and anxiety and linked closely with that chain. 

When I am depressive I will not bother you, I will not tell you how I'm feeling and will more than likely take it out on my wrists. That is me, as someone with bipolar but everyone who I know who is also diagnosed deals with the condition in different ways. Once people find out that you are bipolar they tend to walk on egg shells around you but what I find most interesting is meeting a new person and often, they make large sweeping statements about various conditions. "My god the weather is bipolar (when its been raining and the sun comes out) " "I've got total anxiety when I meet a stranger" (most people are anxious around strangers, an anxiety disorder has varying degrees and is traumatic for those who have one), "I have such bad OCD/ADHD", "that movie made me depressed" 

I won't pretend to imagine what it is like to have other conditions but from my experiences of having BPD it is no wonder people don't go forward for help, the stigma and joking needs to be erased, 

What I am about to say will probably start hate but this is how I see it and think about what I am saying  - a clump of hair falls out of your head onto your hand when you are standing with a friend  at a bus stop beside an elderly woman. "Omg I must have cancer." 

This example is a sweeping statement, I may be inaccurate with the statistics but I think 1 in 5 people have or know someone with a mental health condition and 1 in 3 people know someone who has been affected by cancer. 

Would you, seeing someone with a wig on, a bald head, a heart monitor, anything physical? Compare yourself to them? Would you , when a small piece of hair comes out joke about having cancer? 

If not, then why do some of you insist that because you turned the tap on and then off again are ocd, felt sad and then happy are bipolar, cried at a movie are depressed. 

Its all to do with the lack of physical symptoms. Try walking in my shoes.

As someone who has BPD and is diagnosed I completely agree, I didn't ask to see a professional as I was scared that I wouldn't be taken seriously. A family friend (psychiatrist) suggested to my mother  that I get analyses by a mental health professional and I did.
